groups.title: Laravel Architecture Patterns
groups.question: Your OrderController has grown to 600 lines and checkout logic is also needed by an Artisan command. Explain how you would restructure the code.

followUps.Service Classes and Thin Controllers: Why move business logic into service classes?
followUps.Repository Pattern and Data Access Abstr: When does the repository pattern help, and when is it overkill?

evidence.text: Service classes hold business logic outside controllers.
The same logic can run from controllers, commands and jobs.
Services can be tested without HTTP.
A repository wraps data access behind an interface.
It allows swapping the data source without changing business logic.
With Eloquent, it often adds a layer with little benefit unless the data source really varies.

groups.title: Caching Strategies
groups.question: Product pages run the same queries for every visitor, and after editing a product, related cached pages show old data. Explain your caching strategy.

followUps.remember() and the Cache-Aside Pattern: How do cache tags make invalidation easier?

evidence.text: It returns the cached value if present.
On a miss, it runs the callback and stores the result.
A time-to-live keeps entries from staying stale forever.
Tags group related cache entries, such as everything about one product.
Flushing a tag clears all entries with it at once.
Tags only work with cache stores like Redis and Memcached.

notEnough: Only saying tags label cache entries.

groups.title: Vue 3 Performance Optimization
groups.question: Your Vue orders table re-renders every row when one changes, and the admin charts make the initial download huge. Explain how you would optimise the frontend.

followUps.v-memo and Preventing Unnecessary Re-ren: What does v-memo do for a large list?
followUps.defineAsyncComponent and Code Splitting: How does defineAsyncComponent reduce the first download?

evidence.text: v-memo skips re-rendering a part of the template unless its listed values change.
In large lists, unchanged rows are skipped.
Listing the wrong values can make rows show stale data.
It wraps a dynamic import of the component.
The build puts that component in its own chunk.
The chunk loads only when the component is needed.

groups.title: Redis Advanced Usage
groups.question: Your Vue app polls the API every few seconds for new orders, and Redis connection errors appear under load. Explain how you would push updates and manage Redis connections.

followUps.Redis Pub/Sub for Real-Time Events: How do Redis pub/sub and Laravel Echo replace polling?
followUps.Redis Connection Pooling and Persistent: Why reuse Redis connections, and what happens if you do not?

evidence.text: The server publishes an event when something changes.
A broadcaster like Reverb or Pusher pushes it to connected browsers.
Laravel Echo in the Vue app listens for those events, so no polling is needed.
Laravel connects through phpredis or Predis.
Reusing connections avoids the cost of opening new ones.
Opening too many connections under load can hit Redis limits and cause errors.
